paper.title: PDDFormer: Pairwise Distance Distribution Graph Transformer for Crystal Material Property Prediction
paper.research_summary: The paper introduces WPDDFormer and UPDDFormer—graph transformer models that integrate atom-weighted and unit-cell pairwise distance distribution (PDD) representations into multi-edge crystal graphs to achieve continuous and geometrically complete crystal structure representations. These models are designed to predict material properties (e.g., formation energy, band gap, bulk modulus) from crystal structures while addressing discontinuity and ambiguity caused by atomic vibrations and lattice non-uniqueness. Evaluation shows state-of-the-art performance on Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT benchmark datasets.

tasks.objective: Predict material properties from crystal structures using continuous and geometrically complete graph representations.
input_requirements: crystal structure (unit cell, atomic positions, atomic types, lattice vectors)

evidence.text: Comprehensive evaluation results show that WPDDFormer achieves state-of-the-art predictive accuracy across tasks on benchmark datasets such as the Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT.
We conducted experiments on two material benchmark datasets, namely the Materials Project [Chen et al., 2019] and Jarvis [Choudhary et al., 2020] datasets.

stages.stage_goal: Transform raw crystal structures into continuous and geometrically complete multi-edge graph representations using WPDD or UPDD.
stage_output: multi-edge crystal graphs G = (X, XI, E, PDD)

evidence.text: By introducing PDD, we constructed a general complete and continuous multi-edge crystal graph. In the graph, node features are xi. An edge is established from node j to node i when the Euclidean distance |ej′i|2 between a duplicate of j and i satisfies |ej′i|2 = |pj + k′1l1 + k′2l2 + k′3l3 −pi|2 ≤r, where r ∈R is the cutoff radius. Next, we construct a PDD row for each atom... Therefore, we represent the constructed crystal graph as G = (X, XI, E, PDD).
